qe: If in a code language, PAWAN is written as QBXBO, then how JAMUN will be written in the same language? (PAWAN : QBXBO :: JAMUN : ?)
qh: यदि किसी कूट भाषा में PAWAN को QBXBO लिखा जाता है, तो उसी कूट भाषा में JAMUN को क्या लिखा जाएगा? (PAWAN : QBXBO :: JAMUN : ?)
e:
Method 1 (Forward Pattern (+1 Shift) Shortcut):
Step 1: Letter-by-letter positional shift dekhein:
- P(16) + 1 = 17 (Q)
- A(1) + 1 = 2 (B)
- W(23) + 1 = 24 (X)
- A(1) + 1 = 2 (B)
- N(14) + 1 = 15 (O)
Logic: Sabhi letters me +1 ka forward shift ho raha hai.
Step 2: 'JAMUN' par same +1 shift apply karein:
- J(10) + 1 = 11 (K)
- A(1) + 1 = 2 (B)
- M(13) + 1 = 14 (N)
- U(21) + 1 = 22 (V)
- N(14) + 1 = 15 (O)
Code banega: KBNVO.
Correct option  KBNVO hai.

Method 2 (Option Elimination Method):
- Pehla letter J + 1 = K aayega, isliye 'L' se shuru hone wale options 'LBNWO' and 'LBNVO' seedhe eliminate ho gaye.
- Chautha letter U + 1 = V hona chahiye, 'KBOWO' me 'W' diya hai jo galat hai. Keval 'KBNVO' bachta hai.
Sahi uttar 'KBNVO' hai.

Exam point: code bhasha ka pattern - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: If in a code language, ROAD is written as URDG, then how SWAN will be written in the same language?
qh: यदि किसी कूट भाषा में ROAD को URDG लिखा जाता है, तो उसी कूट भाषा में SWAN को क्या लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Forward Pattern (+3 Shift) Method):
Step 1: 'ROAD' ka positional relation dekhein:
- R(18) + 3 = 21 (U)
- O(15) + 3 = 18 (R)
- A(1) + 3 = 4 (D)
- D(4) + 3 = 7 (G)
Logic: Sabhi letters me +3 add kiya gaya hai.
Step 2: 'SWAN' par +3 apply karein:
- S(19) + 3 = 22 (V)
- W(23) + 3 = 26 (Z)
- A(1) + 3 = 4 (D)
- N(14) + 3 = 17 (Q)
Code: VZDQ.
Correct option  VZDQ hai.

Method 2 (Elimination Method):
- S + 3 = V ('UXDR' eliminate).
- W + 3 = Z ('VXDQ' eliminate).
- A + 3 = D ('VZCQ' me 'C' hai, eliminate).
Keval 'VZDQ' bachta hai.
Sahi uttar 'VZDQ' hai.

Exam point: code bhasha ka pattern - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: If in a code language, ARGUE is written as YPESC, then how DIAGRAM will be written in the same language?
qh: यदि किसी कूट भाषा में ARGUE को YPESC लिखा जाता है, तो उसी भाषा में DIAGRAM को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Constant Backward Shift (-2) Method):
Step 1: 'ARGUE' me letter shift dekhein:
- A(1 ya 27) - 2 = 25 (Y)
- R(18) - 2 = 16 (P)
- G(7) - 2 = 5 (E)
- U(21) - 2 = 19 (S)
- E(5) - 2 = 3 (C)
Logic: Har letter me se 2 minus ho raha hai (-2 shift).
Step 2: 'DIAGRAM' par apply karein:
- D(4) - 2 = 2 (B)
- I(9) - 2 = 7 (G)
- A(27) - 2 = 25 (Y)
- G(7) - 2 = 5 (E)
- R(18) - 2 = 16 (P)
- A(27) - 2 = 25 (Y)
- M(13) - 2 = 11 (K)
Code: BGYEPYK.
Correct option  BGYEPYK hai.

Method 2 (First Letter Elimination Method):
D(4) - 2 = 2 (B). Chaaron options me se sirf 'BGYEPYK' 'B' se shuru ho raha hai, baaki sab bina check kiye eliminate ho jate hain.
Sahi uttar 'BGYEPYK' hai.

Exam point: code bhasha ka pattern - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: If in a code language, DISPLAY is written as BLQSJDW, then how PROJECT will be written in the same language?
qh: यदि किसी कूट भाषा में DISPLAY को BLQSJDW लिखा जाता है, तो उसी भाषा में PROJECT को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Alternate (-2, +3) Pattern Method):
Step 1: 'DISPLAY' ka sequence dekhein:
- D(4) - 2 = 2 (B)
- I(9) + 3 = 12 (L)
- S(19) - 2 = 17 (Q)
- P(16) + 3 = 19 (S)
- L(12) - 2 = 10 (J)
- A(1) + 3 = 4 (D)
- Y(25) - 2 = 23 (W)
Logic: Alternating pattern: -2, +3, -2, +3, -2, +3, -2.
Step 2: 'PROJECT' par apply karein:
- P(16) - 2 = 14 (N)
- R(18) + 3 = 21 (U)
- O(15) - 2 = 13 (M)
- J(10) + 3 = 13 (M)
- E(5) - 2 = 3 (C)
- C(3) + 3 = 6 (F)
- T(20) - 2 = 18 (R)
Code: NUMMCFR.
Correct option  NUMMCFR hai.

Method 2 (Middle Letter Verification Method):
- P - 2 = N, R + 3 = U → Shuruat 'NU' se hogi (Options C aur D eliminate).
- 4th letter J(10) + 3 = 13 (M) hona chahiye, 'NUNMCFR' me 'N' diya hai, isliye (B) eliminate ho gaya.
Sahi uttar 'NUMMCFR' hai.

Exam point: code bhasha ka pattern - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: If in a code language, PRAMOD is written as SODJRA, then how KESHAV will be written in the same language?
qh: यदि किसी कूट भाषा में PRAMOD को SODJRA लिखा जाता है, तो उसी कूट भाषा में KESHAV को क्या लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Alternate (+3, -3) Pattern Method):
Step 1: 'PRAMOD' ka positional shift dekhein:
- P(16) + 3 = 19 (S)
- R(18) - 3 = 15 (O)
- A(1) + 3 = 4 (D)
- M(13) - 3 = 10 (J)
- O(15) + 3 = 18 (R)
- D(4) - 3 = 1 (A)
Logic: Alternate +3, -3, +3, -3, +3, -3 ka shift chal raha hai.
Step 2: 'KESHAV' par apply karein:
- K(11) + 3 = 14 (N)
- E(5) - 3 = 2 (B)
- S(19) + 3 = 22 (V)
- H(8) - 3 = 5 (E)
- A(1) + 3 = 4 (D)
- V(22) - 3 = 19 (S)
Code: NBVEDS.
Correct option  NBVEDS hai.

Method 2 (Option Elimination by Letters):
- K + 3 = N ('MCVEDS' out).
- S + 3 = V ('NBWFDS' me 'W' hai, out).
- H - 3 = E ('NBVFDS' me 'F' diya hai, out). Keval 'NBVEDS' bachta hai.
Sahi uttar 'NBVEDS' hai.

qe: If in a code language, LEADER is written as PIEHIV, then how LIGHT will be written in the same language?
qh: यदि किसी कूट भाषा में LEADER को PIEHIV लिखा जाता है, तो उसी भाषा में LIGHT को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
e:
Method 1 (Constant Forward Shift (+4) Method):
Step 1: 'LEADER' me letter differences check karein:
- L(12) + 4 = 16 (P)
- E(5) + 4 = 9 (I)
- A(1) + 4 = 5 (E)
- D(4) + 4 = 8 (H)
- E(5) + 4 = 9 (I)
- R(18) + 4 = 22 (V)
Logic: Sabhi letters me +4 add ho raha hai.
Step 2: 'LIGHT' par +4 apply karein:
- L(12) + 4 = 16 (P)
- I(9) + 4 = 13 (M)
- G(7) + 4 = 11 (K)
- H(8) + 4 = 12 (L)
- T(20) + 4 = 24 (X)
Code: PMKLX.
Correct option  PMKLX hai.

Method 2 (Elimination Method):
- L + 4 = P (Options C aur D eliminate).
- 4th letter H(8) + 4 = 12 (L) hona chahiye, 'PMKMX' me 4th letter 'M' hai jo galat hai. Isliye 'PMKLX' sahi hai.
Sahi uttar 'PMKLX' hai.

Exam point: prakash ke niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.
